title: Why Watching Quarterly Revenue Is a PM Trap
description:
Most PMs know what a metric is. Fewer know the difference between a metric they can steer with and one that only confirms the past. This Short breaks down leading vs. lagging metrics -- and the common mistake of obsessing over a lagging number week to week, long after the decisions that moved it are already history.

Source lesson:
- https://sigilipelli.github.io/product-manager-mastery-path/level-1/07-metrics-kpis-basics/

#Shorts

beats.narration: Here's a mistake that quietly wrecks product teams: staring at quarterly revenue every single week, waiting for it to move.
Leading metrics -- like weekly active users or onboarding completion -- you can act on right now. Lagging metrics -- like quarterly revenue or churn -- only confirm what already happened.
The trap is treating a lagging metric like it's steerable. By the time quarterly churn actually moves, the decisions that caused it happened months ago.

display.heading: The Trap
display.subheading: The cause is already months old by the time it moves

beats.narration: So use leading metrics to steer your day-to-day decisions, and save lagging metrics for reporting and context.

display.heading: The Fix
display.subheading: Steer with leading. Report with lagging.
